features.evidence: Doctoral / Master's / Bachelor's degree in computer science
features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: This captures the level of formal technical education the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated, or the educational background is unclear.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation in a relevant technical field.
States a master's degree in a relevant technical field.
States a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.evidence: 3, 5, or 7 years testing, maintaining, and launching software products
features.name: Relevant experience depth
features.description: This captures how much directly relevant professional software experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Less than the minimum experience is shown, or the amount of experience is unclear.
Shows roughly minimum-level experience, such as about 2 to 3 years of relevant software work.
Shows solid mid-level experience, such as about 4 to 5 years of relevant software work.
Shows deep experience, such as 6 or more years of relevant software work.

features.name: Production ownership breadth
features.description: This captures the breadth of real production systems the applicant claims to have launched, maintained, or owned.

levels.descriptor: Mentions production work vaguely or not at all.
Shows ownership of 1 to 2 production services or similar limited scope.
Shows ownership of 3 to 4 production services or repeated production responsibility.
Shows ownership of 5 or more production services or extensive repeated production responsibility.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python fluency
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter establishes Python as a real production language rather than a casual secondary tool.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention Python at all.
Mentions Python, but only loosely or as a minor tool.
Shows regular Python use for production services, tooling, or automation.
Shows extensive, production-grade Python ownership, such as typed, tested services or widely used internal tooling.

features.evidence: built with AI where correctness mattered
features.name: Applied AI delivery
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has actually shipped AI-backed functionality and how seriously they treat reliability in those systems.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI interest or exposure, but not shipped work.
Shows shipped AI or LLM-backed features, workflows, or product functionality.
Shows shipped AI systems plus explicit evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or reliability thinking.

features.evidence: conducted formal security assessments ... verifying remediation
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: This captures the depth of hands-on security review experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.evidence: built the automation that triages our vulnerability reports
features.name: Vulnerability automation ownership
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has previously built tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or queue handling.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
Expresses interest in security automation, but gives no evidence of having built it.
Shows direct ownership of tooling for vulnerability intake, triage, classification, or routing.
Shows direct ownership of such tooling and explains its operational impact, such as reduced expert toil or better routing.

features.evidence: Python agents ... Go services keep every action inside well-marked lines
features.name: Agentic architecture experience
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter shows experience designing agent-based systems with bounded actions and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or agent-based system experience is mentioned.
Mentions agents or automation vaguely, without architecture detail.
Describes designing agentic tooling with a recognizable split between agents and supporting services.
Explains the architecture in terms of constraints, permissions, auditability, task decomposition, or other concrete control mechanisms.

features.evidence: replacing a crumbling heuristic with a clean algorithm
features.name: Algorithmic rigor
features.description: This captures whether the letter demonstrates practical strength with data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic skill is mentioned.
Claims algorithmic strength, but without a concrete example.
Gives a specific example of an algorithmic redesign, optimization, or data-structure choice improving a system.
Shows especially strong or repeated algorithmic ownership that appears central to the applicant's system design work.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: This captures the level of formal third-party security validation the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline or fundamentals-oriented credential such as Security+.
Mentions a hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP.

features.evidence: capture-the-flag competitions, near the top of several big ones
features.name: Adversarial practice
features.description: This captures whether the letter shows ongoing offensive-security practice outside ordinary product work.

levels.descriptor: No ongoing adversarial practice is mentioned.
Mentions periodic capture-the-flag participation or light offensive practice.
Shows sustained serious practice, such as regular competition or strong placements.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source project ... reviews, releases
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures the level of responsibility the applicant claims in public software ecosystems.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or one-off upstream fixes.
Shows ongoing contribution or ownership of a public project.
Shows maintainer-level stewardship, such as handling reviews, releases, roadmap, or community questions.

features.evidence: built a fault-tolerant message broker from scratch
features.name: Personal engineering initiative
features.description: This captures the extent to which the letter shows self-directed technical building beyond the day job and how ambitious that work is.

levels.descriptor: No personal project or self-directed technical work is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility, simple app, or curiosity project.
Mentions a substantive personal build that shows real engineering initiative.
Mentions an ambitious systems project with hard technical concerns such as distribution, failover, recovery, or consensus.

features.evidence: make secure development the default rather than the exception
features.name: Platform security mission fit
features.description: This captures how directly the letter aligns the applicant's motivation with secure-by-default, organization-wide security enablement.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic or could apply to almost any software role.
Shows general interest in backend work, infrastructure, or security impact.
Clearly values secure defaults, foundational leverage, or helping developers do the right thing by default.
Frames the work as scaling scarce security expertise across the development lifecycle and shows strong philosophical alignment with that mission.

features.evidence: You are looking for an engineer who can build the systems that scale security work across a large organization
features.name: Role tailoring
features.description: This captures how specifically the letter maps the applicant's background to this exact job rather than to a generic security or backend role.

levels.descriptor: Could be sent to many roles with little or no adaptation to this one.
Mentions the position or company and some relevant keywords, but stays high-level.
Connects experience to several stated qualifications or responsibilities from the posting.
Closely crosswalks past work to the team's specific charter, such as vulnerability handling, developer enablement, Go back ends, Python agents, or AI-related tooling.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: This captures the surface professionalism of the letter's spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

features.evidence: The moment that shaped my engineering priorities was...
features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: This captures whether the letter presents a clear professional story or thesis rather than just a list of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads mainly as an inventory of credentials with little organizing idea.
Shows some motivation or theme, but the connection between past and role is loose.
Presents a clear professional theme, arc, or philosophy linking background to the role.
Delivers a memorable and tightly organized narrative that makes the fit feel intentional.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned to the team
features.name: Evidence concreteness
features.description: This captures how well the letter supports its claims with concrete examples, scope, and outcomes.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad assertions with little supporting detail.
Provides some concrete details, but limited context or results.
Gives several concrete examples of work performed.
Gives concrete examples tied to outcomes, scale, time saved, performance improvement, or other operational effect.
